newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian share volume high, prices dip.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian share volume high, prices dip.

text.p: Trading was active on the Lithuanian stock exchange on Tuesday but dealers said that their informal, in-house indices dipped after rising steadily for several weeks.
Overall market volume was more than five million litas, with bloc trades accounting for the lion's share of trade at 4.5 million litas.

Brokerage Suprema said that its in-house index, which traces 10 companies, including three banks, dipped to 1,065 from 1,074. It says the index accounts for 50 percent of the total stock market capitalisation.
The largest bloc trade today, involving 4.1 million litas, was in iron exporter Medal Komercija.
Dealers said the deal represented a change in ownership in the firm, traded for the first time on the stock exchange.
Central market volume was just over 341,000 litas, with wood processor Medienos Plausas leading the way at more than 100,000 litas. Its shares rose to 10.60 litas from 10.50 litas.

There was just one deal on the T-bill market, worth more than 200,000 litas in three month paper with a yield of 16 percent. That compares with a primary market average yield of 14.03 percent at today's auction of 104-day paper.
